summary: This work proposes a 3D stacked surface-code architecture for measurement-free quantum error correction that eliminates the $O(d)$ SWAP routing overhead required for transversal coupling between logical patches in 2D layouts. Vertical couplers enable constant-depth inter-layer operations, and performance analysis shows the 3D MFEC surface code achieves logical error rates orders of magnitude below standard measurement-based codes in regimes where measurements are slow and noisy.
motivation: Mid-circuit measurements on superconducting platforms are substantially slower and noisier than coherent gates (10–100$\times$ worse), creating a readout floor that limits logical performance of surface codes. While measurement-free QEC (MFEC) avoids repeated measurements, planar implementations require SWAP chains of length $O(d)$ to implement transversal coupling between logical patches, negating the measurement advantage.
method: The architecture stacks three distance-$d$ rotated surface-code patches vertically—encoding $|0\rangle_L$, $|\psi\rangle_L$, and $|+\rangle_L$—with native vertical couplers enabling parallel inter-layer two-qubit gates. A fault-tolerant MFEC protocol uses these vertical transversals for coherent parity mapping and feedback with $O(1)$ depth in $d$. Performance is compared against standard measurement-based surface codes and 2D MFEC variants under a decoherence noise model calibrated to superconducting timescales ($T_1 = 200$ µs, $T_2 = 150$ µs, $t_{2q} = 40$ ns).
result: At break-even decoherence ratio $R_{\mathrm{decoh}} = p_{\mathrm{decoh}}(t_m)/p_{\mathrm{decoh}}(t_{\mathrm{idle,op}}) \sim 30$–200 (depending on distance), the 3D MFEC architecture achieves competitive or superior logical error to measurement-based surface codes, remaining effective to distance $d=11$ while 2D MFEC approaches unit error for $d \geq 7$. At fixed noise ($s=1$, $R_{\mathrm{decoh}}=200$), logical error of 3D MFEC scales only mildly with distance while measurement-based codes saturate near $p_L \sim 0.3$–0.4.
